cands.name: Bale Dalton
cands.bio: Democratic nominee. U.S. Naval Academy graduate, Navy/Navy Reserve helicopter pilot (24 years, now a Reserve captain), worked at the State Department and for Sen. Bill Nelson, later NASA chief of staff. Has not held elected office.
cands.local_ties: Raised in a Central Florida family; campaign based in Sanford (campaign site). Age 45 per ClickOrlando guide.

record.text: Career per campaign site: Navy helicopter pilot (medevac in Kuwait, Hurricane Katrina relief, special-operations support in Iraq and Africa), commanded a Navy special operations support squadron; State Department; aerospace company; NASA chief of staff overseeing about 16,500 employees.

Stated positions: opposes Amendment 3 (property tax), supports abortion rights, bans congressional stock trading, opposes offshore drilling, supports accountability for voucher programs, pathway for Dreamers plus border security.

endorsements.text: Per Wikipedia's District 7 page: DCCC Red to Blue, Blue Dog PAC, 314 Action, VoteVets, Pete Buttigieg, Bill Nelson, Rep. Kathy Castor; post-primary Democratic Majority for Israel and Giffords.
Campaign site lists former Republican Sen. Mel Martinez, Florida AFL-CIO and unions including CWA, SEIU, AFSCME, AFGE and UNITE HERE.
Orlando Sentinel editorial endorsement (Oct 4, 2026) per Wikipedia citation.

cands.name: Ryan Elijah
cands.bio: Republican nominee. Former Orlando TV news anchor/reporter (Emmy winner per Legis1); first run for Florida office, no prior elected service (ran for an Indiana U.S. House seat in 2010 per Wikipedia). Beat incumbent Rep. Cory Mills in the Aug 18, 2026 primary, about 47% to 34%.
cands.local_ties: Florida resident 20 years, 14 in District 7, lives in Seminole County, married with two sons (campaign site). District 7 covers all of Seminole County and southern Volusia County.

record.text: Primary context: incumbent Cory Mills lost renomination amid an ongoing House Ethics Committee investigation (allegations including sexual misconduct and campaign-finance/disclosure issues, which Mills denies) and a restraining order sought by a former girlfriend last fall. Gov. DeSantis said he did not support Mills; Trump had endorsed Mills in 2025 but did not include him in a later list of backed Florida Republicans.
Left his anchor job in April 2026 to challenge Mills; ClickOrlando says Mills was subject of a temporary restraining order last fall, which Mills denies.
Stated positions (ClickOrlando guide): favors property tax relief without cutting public safety, school choice incl. vouchers, voter photo ID, data centers limited to industrial sites.

money_notes.text: Legis1: $301,662 in receipts through June 30, 2026, including a $134,000 candidate loan; the article reported no super PAC or AIPAC spending for either Elijah or Mills in the primary.

endorsements.text: Campaign site lists Gov. Ron DeSantis, Volusia Sheriff Mike Chitwood, Seminole Sheriff Dennis Lemma, Rep. Mike Haridopolos and Rep. Anna Paulina Luna. Roll Call confirms Luna and Haridopolos.

cands.gaps: Owner's five sources NOT searched (search budget exhausted). A Trump general-election endorsement of Elijah appears in Wikipedia's post-primary box and one headline per a campaign-site summary, but I could not open a source, so it is not stated as fact.
